$comment: The platform's document font set. ONE source of truth, read by the
TypeScript layout engine and by the PHP/LibreOffice render side.
Why these files are vendored rather than installed: if the browser and the
renderer do not load the SAME BYTES they shape text differently, page
boundaries diverge, and the on-screen document stops agreeing with the
.docx it produces. An apt point release can change metrics silently, so the
fonts are versioned assets in the repo and the image installs them FROM
here — never the other way round.
Every family is metric-compatible with the Microsoft font a real document
asks for, which is what keeps an inherited .docx from repaginating on open.
All are OFL/Apache licensed: free to embed server-side AND serve to a
browser, which a licensed font typically is not.
The FIRST name in `substitutes` is the one a document should write and the
one the editors OFFER -- `offeredFontFamilies` derives the toolbar from
this file so a family installed here needs no code change to appear. Adding
a family therefore means: drop the four faces in beside this file, add the
entry, rebuild the gotenberg image (docker/gotenberg/Dockerfile) so the
renderer holds the same bytes. All three consumers then agree.
⚠️ MEASURE a candidate before adding it. `metric-compatible` is a claim
fonts make loosely and the failure is silent -- see `metricNotes` below.
Gelasio is NOT in the gotenberg image and was not extracted from it: it
came from the designer's own repository, which is the only source of the
STATIC faces. Google Fonts ships Gelasio as a VARIABLE font, whose hmtx
carries the default instance only -- bold would have measured as regular,
which is exactly the metric lie `FontCatalogue.resolve` refuses to tell.

metricNotes: MEASURED 2026-08-25 against the genuine Georgia on Windows 11, through
this repository's own TrueTypeFont reader, at 40pt unkerned.
ASCII is EXACT in all four faces -- the pangram, 'Handgloves', 'iiiiiiiiii',
'WWWWWWWWWW' and the digits all agree to 0.00%. One exception: 'j' in
BoldItalic is 748 units against Georgia's 747, which is the 0.02px the
pangram disagrees by at 40pt.
⚠️ NOT exact across Latin-1. Per-glyph, of 191 codepoints: Regular and
Bold differ on 2 each, Italic on 8, BoldItalic on 10 -- by codepoint,
so that nothing written here is an invisible character:
U+00B8 (cedilla)  -462 to -522 units, in every face -- the largest
U+00BC U+00BD U+00BE (vulgar fractions) italic +192, bolditalic +260
U+00A2 (cent) bolditalic +180
U+00D3 U+00D6 U+00D8 (O-acute/diaeresis/stroke) italic -28, -1.8%
U+00CC..U+00CE (I-grave..) bolditalic +10, U+00B5 (micro) up to 26
A Swedish, German or Hungarian document set in Georgia italic is the case
that moves; an English one does not move at all.
Kept anyway, and this is the ARITHMETIC for that: the renderer's own
fontconfig was substituting Noto Serif for Georgia, which is +9.31% on a
plain ASCII pangram -- every line of every Georgia document, not a handful
of accented glyphs in italic. Every SHIPPED family sets the bar at 0 of
191 glyphs differing; Gelasio does not meet it and is still an order of
magnitude closer than what it replaced.
⚠️ Measure against a FRESH `npm run build`. An earlier reading of this
same pair reported U+00AD differing by 1282 units and a soft hyphen
falling through to `.notdef` -- both artefacts of a stale `dist/`. The
engine measures U+00AD as zero-width in every face, correctly, and there
is no such defect.

$comment: What a package with NO styles part at all gets. Calibri is what Word's
template writes, so Carlito is ours, and it is what LibreOffice printed
for exactly that package: a .docx holding document.xml and nothing else
embedded Carlito-Regular.
A styles part that EXISTS and states no run defaults is a different case
and is not this one — see `emptyRunDefaults` in style-sheet.ts.
A family nobody ships must resolve through `substitutes` or fail VISIBLY.
A silent swap to a metrically different face is the hardest pagination bug
to diagnose, because the document looks fine and only the page count is
wrong. `fontSynthesis: none` matters for the same reason: a faux-bold has
different advance widths than the real bold face.
